asks: Each tool's description and its inputs' descriptions, written in src/enterich/tools/, say what the tool does, takes, refuses and returns as the code does and its operation's spec says: they are what the agent model reads, and a wrong sentence misleads every agent.
What the README says Enterich is, is not, offers and needs is what the code and the specs do: it is what a deployer reads first.

Each instruction of the configuration guide, for Enterich and for the ERPNext site, gives the behaviour it says when followed: a variable's meaning and effect, a role's rights, a site setting's effect on what the agent user can reach.
A realm set up as the Keycloak guide says yields tokens the token check accepts, and only those: each claim, audience, scope and setting it names is the one the code checks.
What the guides tell reviewers and operators a draft carries, and what Enterich shows the agent of taxes and amounts, is what the code writes and returns.
Each requirement's description in REQ-001 and REQ-002 is what the code does, beyond what its Definition of Done checks; the specs index's area map is the code's.
Each operation's catalogue entry, its description, what it returns per record and the ERPNext calls it lists, is what the code sends and returns; the inputs are checked by tests/repo/test_docs.py.
The arc42 building blocks, runtime and deployment views and each ADR's decision and compliance section are what the code, the image and the workflows do.

out: They say how to work on Enterich, not what Enterich does, and a mistake in them shows when someone follows them.
The security lens's vocabulary (harness/promises.jsonl): that lens reads it against the code.
